# Chimera
Somebody wanted to terraform [textlink="Aerumna" link="Aerumna"] fast. Nobody remembers who, and nobody who knows is admitting it. Their tool was a Letoferol-based biomass that would eat a hostile surface and leave something living behind, grown from a sample nobody could say the source of.
It worked too well. The biomass smothered the whole surface, fouled the air, ran Letoferol through it like blood, and ate the survey team. What it left behind was [color=#c84040]Chimera[/color]: flesh that thinks, hunts, and makes more of itself out of whatever it catches.
## Outbreaks
Chimera reach the wider sector on derelict ships and in sealed cargo. One clawed crewman is enough. The infected turn, the turned grow flesh across the decks, and the flesh plants pustules that burst into ticks.
Both navies keep standing orders for a Chimera outbreak: burn it, space it, and do not let it dock. The Federation and the Dynasty have each, at some point, accused the other of breeding it on purpose.
## Where it is now
After [textlink="the Collapse" link="WFLoreCollapse"] the biomass on Aerumna died back, and the glare pulled away from [textlink="Carcinoma" link="WFLoreCarcinoma"]. That is where the sample came from. Carcinoma is the Chimera's home: one living world, and it was there long before anyone went looking.
